text.text: Spanish Football Federation's competitions committee has rescinded the yellow card shown to Real Madrid defender Ibrahima Konate during the clash with Villarreal, upholding the appeal lodged by the Royal Club. The Frenchman now faces no suspension risk ahead of the eagerly awaited Clasico against Barcelona. Konate had reached four yellow cards this season. One more booking against Sevilla on Sunday and he would have missed the trip to Barcelona. That threat has gone. With the card wiped, the French defender drops back to three yellows and a far safer disciplinary position before the big one. According to the newspaper " Marca ", the committee explained that Konate picked up the booking in the 81st minute against Villarreal, with the referee judging that he had brought down an opponent while competing for the ball and stopped a promising attack. text.text: The Indian ODI skipper, Shubman Gill, won the ICC Player of the Month award on Tuesday. This is the fifth time he has won the prestigious award. Gill was recognised for his brilliant performances against the West Indies in September. He finished ahead of compatriot Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe’s Sikandar Raza.The record for the most ICC Player of the Month awards previously belonged to Pakistan’s Babar Azam, who had won it three times. Babar claimed the honour on three occasions between April 2021 and August 2023. The Indian ODI and Test skipper went past Babar after his Test exploits against England in July 2025. Gill’s latest accolade puts him level with women’s cricketer Hayley Matthews, who has also won it five times. He previously won it in January and September 2023, and then again in February and July 2025. For the uninitiated, the award considers players' performances across all formats.Gill prevailed against strong competitionIndia’s blazing T20I opener, Abhishek Sharma, posed a formidable challenge to Gill. The left-handed batter was in imperious form during the series against Afghanistan. In the first match, he scored 82 off 32 balls, then 39 off 19 in the second.

text.text: Star Indian cricketers Shafali Verma and Shubman Gill were named the ICC Women's and Men's Players of the Month for September 2026. Gill claimed the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza, extending his record as the men's player with the most wins. It is his fifth such honour, following victories in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025 and July 2025. Gill's month was defined by two extraordinary innings against West Indies in the first two ODIs. In Thiruvananthapuram, he made 110 off 108 balls as India chased down 296 with more than eight overs to spare. Three days later in Guwahati, he produced an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, an innings studded with 26 fours and eight sixes, as India hunted down a mammoth 406, their second-highest successful chase in ODI history. His century came off 62 balls, the fastest by an Indian captain in ODIs, while his double century off 117 balls was the fastest in the format's history. It was also the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase, and his 255-run opening stand with Rohit Sharma (101 off 75) was India's highest partnership on home soil. text.text: When Charles Leclerc had a better start than Max Verstappen and claimed the inside line for Turn 1, many in the media centre thought the Monegasque should have held his ground to take the lead. However, Verstappen was on the outside, on the normal racing line that offered slightly more grip, and the Dutchman was prepared to take every risk. Verstappen had already told Autosport a day earlier that second or third place in the drivers' championship would mean nothing to him and that he simply wanted to go all-in for race victories. In other words, Verstappen was willing to risk everything, although that was not even the main reason why Leclerc was unable to complete the move. The reference points drivers use under braking – such as the 150-metre and 100-metre boards – are on the right-hand side approaching Turn 1, but Leclerc could not see them because he was alongside Verstappen. The Ferrari driver had to choose his braking point by instinct and tried to judge it as well as possible. text.text: Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen have explained what happened at the start of Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, where the Ferrari driver had the best launch but failed to outdo his rival. Despite starting from the dirty side of the track – which admittedly wasn’t as dirty as usual given it had rained the day before – Leclerc had his front axle nearly alongside Verstappen’s within seconds. The four-time world champion, however, drove his opponent towards the inside, to the extent that Leclerc’s front wheels briefly exceeded the white line. The Monegasque braked earlier, and Verstappen was able to retain the lead from the outside. “You don't have much time to think in those moments,” Leclerc said. “I just saw that Max had a bit of a difficult start. I had quite a good start, so I went alongside him. Then there wasn't much space anymore, but I would have done exactly the same. “Then it's quite tricky. I was on the left, a little bit behind him, couldn't see the panels on the right, so you lose a little bit all your references because that's normally on the right that you have your references to brake. The Portuguese forward waved a scarf featuring the Saudi flag following Al-Nassr's 3-1 victory over FC Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League Elite, reaffirming his bond with the country and its fans who welcomed him when his career was under scrutiny. There has also been speculation that he could end his playing career in Saudi Arabia. The match was delayed by an hour after an aerial missile alert and explosions were reported across the city. Yemen-based Houthi rebels launched ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, while Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted and destroyed the incoming projectiles. The fixture went ahead once authorities confirmed the danger had passed. Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal in the 42nd minute, taking his career tally to 981 goals during the match in Riyadh. report.text: Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shocked Inter 4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night. Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-born Germany Under-21s forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side. A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go. Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. The Argentinian then gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3-2, but Romeo Vermant once again exposed Inter’s defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side in the third minute of stoppage time. report.text: Home » Sports » Cristiano Ronaldo scores 981st goal in Al Nassr's 3-1 AFC win Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 981st professional goal as Al Nassr secured a 3-1 victory over Neftchi in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Elite on Monday. Ronaldo opened his scoring account nine minutes after Angelo Gabriel's 33rd-minute goal for Al Nassr. Neftchi's Alisher Odilov reduced the deficit in the 51st minute, but an own goal by Anvarjon Gofurov in the 78th minute restored Al Nassr’s two-goal lead, which they maintained until the final whistle. Following the match, Ronaldo wrote on Instagram: "Important win tonight. We keep building." Meanwhile, controversy surrounds Ronaldo’s future with the Portugal national team after he left the squad during the UEFA Nations League. The Portuguese Football Federation has provisionally suspended the 41-year-old and initiated disciplinary proceedings following his departure from the national camp. report.text: In a surprising turn of events at the Shanghai Masters, Zizou Bergs delivered a stunning performance by defeating second-seeded Carlos Alcaraz with a score of 7-5, 7-6 (4), propelling himself into the fourth round of the prestigious tournament. This victory marks a significant milestone in Bergs’ young career as he converted his first match point with an impressive ninth ace, securing what is arguably the biggest win of his professional journey thus far. This match was the second encounter between Bergs and Alcaraz on the ATP tour, with the Belgian marking his first victory against the tournament favorite. Post-match, Bergs expressed a blend of respect and newfound confidence regarding competing against top players, acknowledging how his reverence for them has sometimes hindered his performance. "I have too much respect for (top players), which is part of my culture and I’m proud of that. But it gets a little bit in the way when you have to play them," he remarked. reports.headline: Warriors win over Lakers in Vegas, 101-89

report.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor.
